extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents and applicants)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedures for examination of U.S. patent applications, including requisites of the application, search obligations, requirements for information (37 CFR 1.105), replies and timing, handling of informal disclosures, and expungement of submitted materials (37 CFR 1.59).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory authority for examination (35 U.S.C. 131)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall cause an examination to be made of the application and the alleged new invention; and if on such examination it appears that the applicant is entitled to a patent under the law, the Director shall issue a patent therefor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The main conditions precedent to the grant of a patent are set forth in 35 U.S.C. 101, 102 and 103. See related MPEP sections for form paragraphs (e.g., 7.04 copies 35 U.S.C. 101; MPEP § 706.03(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability requirements (35 U.S.C. 101/102/103)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whoever invents or discovers any new and useful process, machine, manufacture, or composition of matter, or any new and useful improvement thereof, may obtain a patent therefor, subject to the conditions and requirements of this title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These statutory provisions define patentable subject matter and the substantive criteria (novelty, nonobviousness, utility) that the examiner must apply during examination. See MPEP chapters referenced for further detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions (35 U.S.C. 100)
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutory definitions used in the title (e.g., 'invention' means invention or discovery; 'process' means process, art, or method and includes a new use of a known process; 'United States' includes territories and possessions; 'patentee' includes successors in title).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should apply these definitions when interpreting application terms and statutory provisions during examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requisites of the application (35 U.S.C. 111(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: When a new application is assigned in the Technology Center, the examiner should review the contents of the application to determine if the application meets the requirements of 35 U.S.C. 111(a). Matters affecting the filing date or abandonment (e.g., lack of an oath/declaration, filing fee, or claims) should be checked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the application meets requisites set forth in MPEP Chapter 600 (formal matters, completeness and clarity of disclosure). If requisites are not met, applicant may be called upon for necessary amendments which must not include new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for obviously informal cases
rubrics_metrics.description: When it is impractical to give a complete action on the merits because of an informal or insufficient disclosure, follow a limited procedure: (A) make a reasonable search based on what can be understood; (B) point out informalities and drawing deficiencies via attachments; (C) require specification revision to idiomatic English and U.S. practice; (D) reject informal claims as failing to define the invention under 35 U.S.C. 112.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If disclosure is incomprehensible to preclude a reasonable search, clearly inform applicant no search was made. Treat multiple obviously informal claims as a single claim for fee and examination purposes. Urge preliminary amendments (preferably within 3 months) but exclude new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unconventional terminology — cannot be examined (form paragraph 7.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: If terminology is so different from that generally accepted in the art that a proper search cannot be made, use form paragraph 7.01 requiring clarification or correlation with art-accepted terminology so that comparison with prior art can be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide specific indication of problematic terminology/properties/units and pages. Set a shortened statutory period for reply (ONE MONTH or THIRTY DAYS, whichever is longer). See MPEP § 702.01 and § 704.01 for usage notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search obligations and prior examiner deference
rubrics_metrics.description: After reading the specification and claims, the examiner searches the prior art; the invention should be thoroughly understood before a search. When acting on an application previously acted on by another examiner, give full faith and credit to the previous examiner's search and action unless there is a clear error or knowledge of other prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not take an entirely new approach or make a new search merely in hope of finding something; see MPEP § 904–904.03 and MPEP § 719.05 for guidance on prior examiner's work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to require information (37 CFR 1.105)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the course of examining or treating a matter, the examiner or other Office employee may require the submission, from individuals identified under § 1.56(c) or any assignee, of such information as may be reasonably necessary to properly examine or treat the matter (examples follow).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The scope extends to assignees where an assignee has asserted right to prosecute. The authority arises from 35 U.S.C. 131 and 132 and is exercised consistent with Technology Center policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of information that may be required under 1.105
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples include: particularly relevant commercial databases known to inventors; whether a search was made and what was searched; copies of non-patent literature/patents/publications related to claimed invention; information used to draft the application or in the invention process; identification of what is being improved; identification of any use of the claimed invention known at filing; technical information known to applicant concerning related art, disclosure, claimed subject matter, or facts pertinent to patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements may seek factual information only (not opinions), and may be presented as interrogatories, stipulations, or specific questions. A reply stating information is unknown or not readily available may be accepted as complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: factual information and reasonable basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Information required must be factual and reasonably necessary to properly examine or treat the matter; there must be a reasonable basis that the information would aid examination. The scope should be narrowly defined and based on the examiner's reasonable basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 1.105 is not a substitute for examiner search—examiner must still make their own search per MPEP § 704.01 and § 904 et seq. The reasonable necessity criteria is met when (A) claimed subject matter cannot be adequately searched by class/keyword, or (B) the application file or lack of relevant prior art suggests applicant likely has relevant information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of information reasonably required (detailed list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-exhaustive examples: (A) name/citation of relevant indexed journal or treatise; (B) trade name of goods/services embodying claimed subject matter; (C)-(D) citations/copies of advertising or journal articles; (E)-(F) trade names/providers/analyses of competing goods/services; (G) identification of pending/abandoned applications by inventor or assignee disclosing similar subject matter; (H) reply to a protest under 37 CFR 1.291; (I) explanation of technical material in a publication; (J)-(L) identification of changes in reformatted continuing applications, mark-ups for CIPs, comments on new Federal Circuit decisions; (M)-(S) publication dates, derivation questions, art related to applicant's invention, accuracy of examiner's analysis, means-plus-function support clarifications; (S) interrogatories or stipulations about common technical features, support for means/steps-plus-function claims, portions of disclosure providing written description/enablement, meanings of claim terms, portions corresponding to admitted prior art, facts related to public use or sale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these examples to narrowly focus requirements. Where support for a means-plus-function claim is unclear, inquiry may lead to rejections under 35 U.S.C. 112 (written description/definiteness) if support cannot be shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: When a requirement for information may be made (timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: A requirement under 37 CFR 1.105 is discretionary and may be made at any time once necessity is recognized; optimum time is prior to or with a first action on the merits because examiner has maximum opportunity to consider reply. Ordinarily, a request should not be made with or after a final rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Circumstances: (I) prior to first action — appropriate for new tech areas without good art pools (consider factors A–F); (II) with first action on the merits — may combine when file or lack of art justifies asking for info; not appropriate with allowance or Ex parte Quayle actions; (III) after first action — rarely appropriate and only where further action by examiner will follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replies to a requirement for information — completeness and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Replies must be complete and filed within the time period set (including any extensions). Failure to reply within the set time will result in abandonment of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All replies should be checked for completeness. An incomplete reply can be completed within the original time period (including extensions). Supplemental replies after expiration must comply with other rules for submissions. Extensions may be granted under 37 CFR 1.136(a) where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship of 1.105 requirements to duty of disclosure (37 CFR 1.56)
rubrics_metrics.description: The duty of candor and good faith under 37 CFR 1.56 applies to replies to 1.105 requirements; however, 1.56's threshold (material to patentability) is higher than 1.105's threshold (reasonable necessity to examination).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under 1.105 the Office can compel submission of information reasonably necessary to examination even if applicant would not consider it material. Applicant must make reasonable inquiry to obtain facts known or readily obtainable but is not required to independently discover facts (e.g., by experimentation).

rubrics_metrics.name: What constitutes a complete reply to 1.105
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete reply responds to each enumerated requirement by either providing the requested information or stating that the information is unknown and/or not readily available to the party from which it was requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant need not distinguish between 'unknown' and 'not readily available.' A reply that such information is unknown/not readily available will generally be sufficient unless it is clear applicant misunderstood the requirement or the reply is ambiguous. A follow-up requirement may be made where reasonable and warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of an incomplete reply to 1.105
rubrics_metrics.description: An incomplete reply in a pending application or reexamination is handled like an amendment not fully responsive to a non-final Office action (see 37 CFR 1.135(c) and MPEP § 714.03).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the reply is a bona fide reply, use form paragraph 7.95. The practice gives a TIME PERIOD of ONE (1) MONTH or THIRTY (30) DAYS from mailing to supply omissions/corrections to avoid abandonment; extensions under 1.136(a) may be granted. No extension where deliberate omission or application subject to a final Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time periods for reply and extension rules (37 CFR 1.135/1.136)
rubrics_metrics.description: Replies or failures to reply to 1.105 requirements are governed by 37 CFR 1.135 and 1.136. Requirements made without an action on the merits should set a shortened statutory period of two months; applicant may extend up to six months under 1.136(a). Requirements sent with an Office action receive the same period as that action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A requirement under 1.105 is an Office action under 35 U.S.C. 132 for patent term adjustment purposes (see MPEP § 2730).

rubrics_metrics.name: Making a requirement for information — scope and format
rubrics_metrics.description: A requirement under 37 CFR 1.105 should be narrowly specified and limited in scope because it imposes substantial burden on applicant and examiner; it is only warranted where the benefit exceeds the burden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use prescribed form paragraphs (e.g., 7.95 for bona fide non-responsive amendments) and clearly focus the reason and scope of expected response. The requirement may be included in an Office action or sent separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: General rule on expungement of information (37 CFR 1.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: Information in an application will not be expunged except as provided in 37 CFR 1.59(b). Information forming part of the original disclosure (written specification, claims, drawings, preliminary amendments specifically incorporated in an executed oath/declaration) will not be expunged from the file wrapper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An applicant may request expungement of other information by filing a petition under 37 CFR 1.59(b) with the required fee and establishing to the Director's satisfaction that expungement is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to expunge — factors for granting (MPEP § 724.05 items)
rubrics_metrics.description: Expungement of information initially submitted under MPEP § 724.02 or that should have been submitted in a sealed envelope is appropriate when petitioner complies with enumerated items (including that information contains trade secret/proprietary/protected material not public; unintentional submission causing irreparable harm; information not made public; commitment to retain returned information; established to Director that info not material; petition fee included).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where information was inadvertently submitted, items (A)-(F) in MPEP § 724.05 paragraph II must be satisfied. Unidentified trade-secret/proprietary information in an IDS may be placed in an Office prior art search file and may not be retrievable—petition evaluated case-by-case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of petitions to expunge — incorrect application and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: If information was placed in an incorrect application, a petition may request expungement rather than transfer; however, if the Office can determine the correct file (identifying information present), the Office will transfer the papers to the correct application without a petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions on petitions are often held in abeyance until allowance, mailing of an Ex parte Quayle action, or application abandonment, at which time the petition will be decided (use form paragraph 7.204). If information was submitted outside MPEP § 724.02/IDS, petition should be sent to Office of Petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision on petition to expunge — grant/dismiss criteria and form paragraphs
rubrics_metrics.description: If petition is granted, use form paragraph 7.205; if petition is dismissed, use 7.206 followed by specific paragraphs 7.207–7.213 to state reasons (e.g., lack of fee; information material to patentability; information made public; no commitment to retain; no clear trade-secret/proprietary/unintentional statement; unclear identification of information; petition not by party in interest who submitted information).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When granting expungement, petitioner must retain expunged materials for life of any patent issuing from the application. 'Materiality' is defined as any information examiner considers important to a determination of patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention obligation when expungement granted
rubrics_metrics.description: When a petition to expunge is granted, applicant is required to retain the expunged material(s) for the life of any patent which issues on the affected application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This retention requirement accompanies the grant and is intended so that the expunged materials remain available notwithstanding removal from the official file; see form paragraph 7.205.
